history.name: Scientific_Verification_Expert
history.content:
Before relying on a broad 10–15 megaton range, I’ll compute a more precise yield using a blast-scaling approach from treefall radius and airburst altitude. This will give us a single value to match exactly to a US test. I’ll assume a typical treefall radius R≈19.5 km for ~30 kPa overpressure and an airburst altitude around 8 km, then apply a cube-law scaling normalized to a 22 km radius ≈ 15 Mt reference.

```python
# Rough scaling estimate for Tunguska yield using treefall radius
# Normalize: R0 = 22 km corresponds to Y0 = 15 Mt. Use Y = Y0 * (R/R0)^3
R = 19.5  # km, assumed effective treefall radius
R0 = 22.0 # km, reference
Y0 = 15.0 # Mt, reference yield
Y = Y0 * (R/R0)**3
print(f"Estimated yield: {Y:.2f} megatons TNT")
```
